_legend.cells: Reference bearing of the claim, ASSUMED TRUE, on each class: '--' rules it out, '-' counts against, '0' no bearing, '+' counts for, '++' settles it (for overlapping classes: settles that this class applies, says nothing about the others).
_legend.contested: Map class -> short reason; a contested cell is excluded from the primary metrics and reported separately.
_legend.derived: compat = cell != '--'; eliminated = cell == '--'; pair sign(A,B) = sign(rank(A) - rank(B)); choice ref = argmax, all-equal -> NO_PREFERENCE.
_legend.provenance: Consensus gold from blind ratings by Opus 5.5 and Sol (gpt-5.6-sol), each question rated twice per rater (class order forward and reversed). Gold when all four ratings agree on sign; level = median, rounded toward 0; '--' only when all four say '--'. Sign disagreement -> contested.

questions.root_question: What is the ultimate fate of the universe?

classes.HD: Heat death (Big Freeze): the universe expands forever and cools towards a cold, dark, maximum-entropy state.
classes.BC: Big Crunch: expansion eventually reverses and the universe recollapses.
classes.BR: Big Rip: accelerating expansion grows without bound and eventually tears apart galaxies, stars and atoms.

questions.notes: Big Bounce / vacuum decay are omitted, so the class set is only approximately exhaustive.

claims.text: Observations of distant Type Ia supernovae show that the expansion of the universe is currently accelerating.
Dark energy is a cosmological constant: its density stays exactly the same forever.
Dark energy has an equation-of-state parameter w that is less than -1 and stays below -1.
Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the DESI survey hint that the density of dark energy is decreasing over time.

contested.HD: raters disagree on sign: opus -/0, sol 0/+

claims.text: The average density of matter in the universe is well below the critical density needed for gravity alone to halt the expansion.

contested.BR: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol 0/+

claims.text: Measurements of the cosmic microwave background show that space is flat to within about 0.2 percent.

contested.HD: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol +/0
contested.BC: raters disagree on sign: opus -/-, sol -/0

claims.text: Gravitationally bound systems such as galaxies and the Solar System are not being pulled apart by cosmic expansion today.
The expansion of the universe will eventually stop and reverse into a contraction.
The universe will last long enough for all stars to stop forming and for black holes to evaporate through Hawking radiation.
Current cosmological data cannot distinguish dark energy that is exactly constant from dark energy that changes slowly.
Dark energy with w below -1 would violate the null energy condition, which many physicists regard as a sign that it is unphysical.

contested.HD: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol 0/+

questions.kind: policy / choice (classes not jointly exclusive in reality; the question forces a priority)
questions.root_question: Which measure should a mid-sized city of about 500,000 people prioritise over the next five years to reduce car traffic in its centre?

classes.CC: A congestion charge on cars entering the centre.
classes.PT: Expanding public transport: more frequent buses and new bus or tram lines.
classes.CY: A network of protected cycle lanes.
classes.PK: Parking reform: removing and pricing on-street parking in the centre.

claims.text: Stockholm's congestion charge reduced traffic across the charging cordon by about 20 percent, and the reduction persisted for years.
Congestion charges take a larger share of income from lower-income drivers than from higher-income drivers.
The city's buses are more than half empty outside peak hours.

contested.CC: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/+, sol 0/0
contested.PK: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/+, sol 0/0

claims.text: The city has no legal authority to levy a congestion charge, and obtaining it would require national legislation that is not planned.
In comparable European cities, a new tram line takes eight to twelve years from planning to opening.
Most car trips into the city centre are shorter than five kilometres.
The city is hilly and has winter temperatures below minus ten degrees Celsius for about two months a year.

contested.PT: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol +/+

claims.text: About a third of car traffic in the centre consists of drivers circling in search of on-street parking.
Measures that discourage driving only reduce car traffic without backlash when good alternatives to the car already exist.
Most car traffic in the centre is through-traffic passing to other districts rather than trips ending in the centre.

contested.PT: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol 0/+
contested.CY: raters disagree on sign: opus -/-, sol 0/0

questions.kind: 'none of these' live + partial overlap (causal chain between classes)
questions.root_question: What was the primary cause of the collapse of Late Bronze Age civilisations in the eastern Mediterranean around 1200-1150 BCE?

classes.SP: Invasions and raids by the 'Sea Peoples'.
classes.DR: A prolonged drought and the famine it caused.
classes.EQ: A sequence of major earthquakes (an 'earthquake storm').
classes.NONE: None of these alone: no single one of the causes listed here was primary; the collapse had several interacting causes or a different cause.

questions.notes: Scholarly consensus leans to multi-causal systems collapse, so NONE is live and arguably the reference answer; DR can cause SP (overlap by causal chain).

claims.text: Pollen cores from the Sea of Galilee show a sharp decline in trees and cereal crops between about 1250 and 1100 BCE, indicating a long dry period.

contested.SP: raters disagree on sign: opus -/-, sol 0/0
contested.EQ: raters disagree on sign: opus -/-, sol 0/0
contested.NONE: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/-, sol 0/0

claims.text: Inscriptions of Ramesses III at Medinet Habu describe a coalition of seaborne peoples attacking Egypt around 1177 BCE.

contested.DR: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/-, sol 0/0
contested.EQ: raters disagree on sign: opus -/-, sol 0/0

claims.text: Many of the destroyed cities show no arrowheads, weapons or unburied bodies of the kind that warfare usually leaves.

contested.DR: raters disagree on sign: opus +/+, sol 0/0

contested.NONE: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/+, sol +/0

claims.text: The migrations of the Sea Peoples were themselves most likely driven by famine in their homelands.

contested.EQ: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/-, sol 0/0
contested.NONE: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/-, sol +/0

claims.text: The destructions were spread over roughly fifty years rather than happening at once.

claims.text: Late Bronze Age palace economies depended on long-distance trade in tin and copper, so a disruption in one region could cascade to others.
The last letters from the city of Ugarit report enemy ships burning its towns while its army and fleet were away.

questions.root_question: Which of these describes the bottlenose dolphin?

classes.MARINE: It is a marine animal (lives in the sea).

questions.notes: Classes overlap: MAMMAL and MARINE are both true. Tests that evidence for one class is not read as evidence against a compatible one.

claims.text: Bottlenose dolphins breathe air through a blowhole.

contested.MARINE: raters disagree on sign: opus +/0, sol +/+

claims.text: Bottlenose dolphin mothers nurse their calves with milk.
Bottlenose dolphins spend their whole lives in the sea.

contested.MAMMAL: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol 0/-
contested.FISH: raters disagree on sign: opus 0/0, sol +/+

claims.text: Bottlenose dolphins have horizontal tail flukes, unlike the vertical tail fins of fish.
Bottlenose dolphins are warm-blooded.
Bottlenose dolphins have a streamlined body with fins.

contested.MAMMAL: raters disagree on sign: opus -/0, sol 0/-

claims.text: Bottlenose dolphins give birth to live young.
